concepts.name: Git Worktree
concepts.description: A git worktree checks out another branch of the same repository into a separate directory, sharing one object store, so parallel tasks stay isolated without a second clone.
concepts.context: git worktree add -b "$BRANCH" "../$REPO-worktrees/$SLUG" origin/main in scripts/new-task.sh gives each task its own directory and branch

concepts.name: Shell Working Directory
concepts.description: A script's cd changes the directory for every later command in that script, so steps like npm install and git config act on the new location. It does not change the caller's shell.
concepts.context: cd "../$REPO-worktrees/$SLUG" in scripts/new-task.sh makes the following npm install and git config run inside the new worktree

concepts.name: Per-Worktree Dependencies
concepts.description: Untracked files such as node_modules are not shared between worktrees, so each new worktree needs its own dependency install before builds or tests will run.
concepts.context: npm install in scripts/new-task.sh runs in the fresh worktree, which starts with no node_modules
git fetch origin main, then origin/main as the start point in scripts/new-task.sh, so new task branches start from the latest upstream commit rather than a stale local main
concepts.description: Fetching updates the remote-tracking ref origin/main, and branching from that ref instead of local main starts a new branch from the latest upstream commit.

concepts.context: git config core.hooksPath .githooks in scripts/new-task.sh wires the repo's committed hooks into the new worktree
concepts.description: core.hooksPath points git at a hooks directory kept in the repository, so hooks are versioned and shared, but each clone or worktree must set the path itself because git config is not committed.

concepts.name: Git Worktree
concepts.description: A linked working directory attached to the same repository, letting a new branch be checked out in its own folder without disturbing the main checkout.
concepts.context: git worktree add -b "$BRANCH" "../$REPO-worktrees/$SLUG" origin/main in scripts/new-task.sh creates an isolated branch folder beside the repo

concepts.name: Worktree Dependency Setup
concepts.description: Each worktree has its own working files and node_modules, so dependencies must be installed per worktree before tests or builds run.
concepts.context: cd into the new worktree then npm install in scripts/new-task.sh, because the fresh folder has no node_modules
git fetch origin main runs before the worktree add, which then bases the branch on origin/main rather than local main in scripts/new-task.sh

concepts.description: The core.hooksPath setting points git at a versioned hooks directory instead of the untracked .git/hooks, so a team shares the same hooks.
concepts.context: git config core.hooksPath .githooks in scripts/new-task.sh enables the repo's committed hooks inside the new worktree, since hooks aren't copied with a checkout

concepts.name: Mutation Testing
concepts.description: Judging test quality by injecting small code changes (mutants) and checking whether the tests fail. Surviving mutants reveal assertions that don't actually protect behavior, which line coverage alone misses.
concepts.context: stryker.conf.json mutates src/**/*.ts but excludes *.test.ts, so mutants are injected only into production code, not the tests that must catch them

concepts.name: Mutation Score Thresholds
concepts.description: Stryker's high, low and break thresholds grade the mutation score. High and low colour the report, and break fails the run when the score drops below it, which turns the score into a CI gate.
concepts.context: thresholds in stryker.conf.json set high 90, low 70 and break 60, so a mutation score under 60 exits non-zero and fails the run

concepts.name: Vitest Test Runner
concepts.description: Stryker runs the existing test suite against each mutant through a runner plugin. The testRunner setting picks which framework executes those tests.
concepts.context: testRunner is set to vitest in stryker.conf.json so each mutant of src/**/*.ts is checked by the project's Vitest tests

concepts.name: Test Report Reporters
concepts.description: Reporters decide how mutation results are output. A terminal table gives quick feedback, and an HTML report lets you inspect each surviving mutant in the source.
concepts.context: reporters in stryker.conf.json combines clear-text for terminal output with html for a browsable per-file report of surviving mutants

concepts.name: Mutation Testing
concepts.description: Judging test quality by injecting small code changes (mutants) and checking that the tests fail. Surviving mutants reveal assertions that do not really verify behavior.
concepts.context: configured Stryker in stryker.conf.json to mutate src/**/*.ts so weak tests show up as surviving mutants

concepts.name: Stryker Config
concepts.description: Stryker's JSON config picks which files get mutated, which test runner kills the mutants, and which reporters write the results.
concepts.context: stryker.conf.json sets testRunner to vitest and reporters to clear-text and html

concepts.name: Vitest Runner
concepts.description: Stryker runs the project's existing test suite through a plugin for the test runner, here Vitest, to decide whether each mutant is killed or survives.
concepts.context: testRunner set to vitest in stryker.conf.json

concepts.name: Score Thresholds
concepts.description: The high, low and break values map a mutation score to a status. A score below break fails the run, so the threshold acts as a quality gate in CI.
concepts.context: thresholds in stryker.conf.json are high 90, low 70, break 60, so a score under 60 fails the run

concepts.name: Mutation Scope Globs
concepts.description: Glob patterns with ! negation choose which source files are mutated. Leaving out test files stops Stryker from mutating the tests that are meant to catch mutants.
concepts.context: mutate array in stryker.conf.json includes src/**/*.ts and excludes !src/**/*.test.ts

concepts.name: Custom Hook
concepts.description: A function starting with 'use' that wraps stateful and effect logic so components can reuse it. Here useOnline returns a boolean connectivity flag.
concepts.context: useOnline() in src/useOnline.ts packages online/offline state into a reusable hook returning a boolean

concepts.name: Effect Cleanup
concepts.description: The function returned from useEffect runs on unmount or before re-run, undoing the subscription set up by the effect so listeners do not leak.
concepts.context: useEffect in src/useOnline.ts returns a function calling removeEventListener for 'online' and 'offline' on window

concepts.name: DOM Event Listeners
concepts.description: Registering and removing handlers on browser targets with addEventListener and removeEventListener, which needs the same function reference to detach.
concepts.context: on and off are named consts in src/useOnline.ts so the exact references passed to addEventListener can be removed in cleanup

concepts.name: Online Status API
concepts.description: navigator.onLine reports whether the browser thinks it has a network connection, and window fires 'online' and 'offline' events when it changes. It signals link state, not real reachability.
concepts.context: useState(navigator.onLine) seeds the initial value in src/useOnline.ts, then the online/offline events keep it updated

concepts.name: Dependency Array
concepts.description: The second argument to useEffect controls when it re-runs; an empty array means set up once on mount and clean up on unmount.
concepts.context: useEffect(..., []) in src/useOnline.ts subscribes once because the handlers only call stable state setters

concepts.name: React state
concepts.description: useState keeps a value between renders; its initial argument is used only on the first render and should mirror the true starting condition of any external state, like navigator.onLine.
concepts.context: useState(navigator.onLine) in src/useOnline.ts starts from the browser's current connectivity rather than assuming true

concepts.name: Custom Hook
concepts.description: A function starting with 'use' that wraps stateful logic and effects so components can reuse it. Here useOnline exposes the browser's connectivity as a boolean.
concepts.context: extracted online/offline tracking into useOnline() in src/useOnline.ts returning a single boolean

concepts.name: DOM Event Listeners
concepts.description: Subscribing to window events with addEventListener and unsubscribing with removeEventListener using the same function reference.
concepts.context: named on/off handlers in src/useOnline.ts so removeEventListener receives the identical references passed to addEventListener

concepts.name: Navigator Online
concepts.description: navigator.onLine gives the browser's current connectivity guess, and the online/offline events signal changes. It reports network presence, not whether a server is reachable.
concepts.context: seeded useState with navigator.onLine in src/useOnline.ts, then kept it current from the online/offline events
returned a cleanup in src/useOnline.ts that removes both the 'online' and 'offline' window listeners
concepts.description: The function returned from useEffect runs on unmount or before the next run, so window listeners added in the effect are removed and do not leak.

concepts.context: passed [] in src/useOnline.ts because the handlers only call the stable setOnline setter, so the effect subscribes once on mount
concepts.description: The dependency array is a correctness contract: an empty array is right here because the effect reads no props or state, only the stable setter.

concepts.name: Express Middleware
concepts.description: A function (req, res, next) registered with app.use that runs on every request in order, and either ends the response or calls next() to pass control on.
concepts.context: app.use middleware in server/cors.ts calls next() for non-OPTIONS requests so later routes still run

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.description: Browsers block cross-origin reads unless the server opts in with Access-Control headers; non-simple requests are preceded by an OPTIONS preflight. Covers the allow-origin and allow-headers response headers, answering the preflight with a 204, and pinning a single trusted origin instead of a wildcard when an authorization header is allowed.
concepts.context: set Access-Control-Allow-Origin to ALLOWED_ORIGIN, allow content-type and authorization headers, and short-circuit OPTIONS preflight with sendStatus(204) in server/cors.ts

concepts.name: Express Middleware
concepts.description: Functions run in order for each request that either end the response or call next() to pass control down the chain.
concepts.context: app.use((req, res, next) => ...) in server/cors.ts ends OPTIONS with 204 and calls next() for every other request

concepts.name: CORS
concepts.description: Browsers block cross-origin reads unless the server opts in with Access-Control headers; non-simple requests are preceded by an OPTIONS preflight. Here the server allows one origin and the content-type and authorization request headers, and answers preflights itself.
concepts.context: set Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Allow-Headers and answer OPTIONS preflights with 204 in the middleware in server/cors.ts

concepts.name: Origin Allowlist
concepts.description: Restricting cross-origin access to one trusted origin instead of a wildcard, which matters when requests carry an Authorization header.
concepts.context: ALLOWED_ORIGIN constant used instead of '*' in server/cors.ts because the API accepts an authorization header
